verdict.rationale: Sentry's own developer docs say you can run all of Sentry on your own server for free, with public source and a maintained out-of-the-box self-hosted setup. Several long-term self-hosters confirm it works in production via install.sh or Helm, and describe it as rock-solid once running. Missing for 10: any support guarantee for the self-hosted setup (the docs say no guarantees or dedicated support), lighter resource needs (users report 16GB+ RAM, growing containers and Kafka/Redis tuning), and timely release parity (self-hosted releases lag SaaS launches).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
In addition to making its source code available publicly, Sentry offers and maintains a minimal setup that works out-of-the-box for simple use cases.
Has self-hosted Sentry for over 10 years: git clone, edit one or two config files, run ./install.sh.
